grammar: n. 引体向上。可数，复数 pull-ups；作定语时常写 pull-up bar（单杠）。
collocations: do a pull-up; do ten pull-ups; a pull-up bar
commonMistake: pull-up 是名词，复数在整个复合词后加 -s：pull-ups；动词短语“拉起”则写 pull up。

example.english: I could do five pull-ups after weeks of training.
example.chinese: 训练了几周后，我能做五个引体向上。

application.prompt: At the fitness test, Mia hung from the bar and lifted her chin above it. She completed one ___. A. pull-up B. relay
application.solution: A。解析：悬挂在杠上并把下巴拉过横杠是 pull-up（引体向上）。

grammar: n. 接力赛；接力。可数，复数 relays；relay race 指接力赛，relay 作动词时表示转交或转播。
collocations: a relay race; run a relay; a relay team
commonMistake: relay 表示比赛时，选手要依次接棒；接力赛不是每位选手同时起跑的个人赛。

example.english: Our relay team won the race by two seconds.
example.chinese: 我们的接力队以两秒优势赢得了比赛。

application.prompt: Four runners each covered one part of the race and passed a baton to the next teammate. They competed in a ___. A. marathon B. relay
application.solution: B。解析：多名跑者依次跑一段并交接接力棒，是 relay（接力赛）。

grammar: n. 推铅球（比赛）。可作 shot put（常见分写形式），通常作单数项目名称。
collocations: the shot-put event; compete in the shot put; a shot-put athlete
commonMistake: shot-put 是田径投掷项目，动作是从肩部推出重球；不是把球像棒球一样投出去。

example.english: Liu entered the shot-put event at the school sports meet.
example.chinese: 刘参加了学校运动会的推铅球项目。

application.prompt: The athlete held a heavy metal ball near his neck and pushed it as far as he could. Which event was this? A. shot-put B. shot-putter
application.solution: A。解析：从肩部推出重球的项目是 shot-put（推铅球）；shot-putter 指运动员。

grammar: n. 拳击（运动）。通常不可数；boxer 指拳击手，boxing match 指拳击比赛。
collocations: learn boxing; a boxing match; a professional boxer
commonMistake: 表示拳击这项运动通常说 boxing，不加 a；指一场比赛时可说 a boxing match。

example.english: My uncle began boxing when he was in high school.
example.chinese: 我叔叔高中时开始练拳击。

application.prompt: The two athletes wore gloves and took turns punching inside a ring. The sport was ___. A. fencing B. boxing
application.solution: B。解析：戴拳击手套、在拳台上对打的运动是 boxing（拳击）。

grammar: n. 比赛；竞赛；竞争。动词 compete；形容词 competitive；复数 competitions。
collocations: enter a competition; win a competition; a sports competition
commonMistake: competition 是比赛或竞争，competitor 是参赛者；表示“参加比赛”用 compete in/at a competition。

example.english: The school held a swimming competition on Friday.
example.chinese: 学校周五举办了一场游泳比赛。

application.prompt: More than 100 students entered the event, and the fastest swimmer won a prize. It was a swimming ___. A. competition B. competitor
application.solution: A。解析：有多人参赛并决出胜者的活动是 competition（比赛）；competitor 是选手。

grammar: n. 预赛；选拔赛；试用。可数，复数 tryouts；常用于美式英语，英式英语也常写 trial。
collocations: a team tryout; go to a tryout; hold tryouts for the team
commonMistake: tryout 是名词“选拔赛”；动词短语 try out 表示参加选拔或试用，书写时分开。

example.english: Several students came to the basketball tryout after school.
example.chinese: 放学后，几名学生来参加篮球队选拔。

application.prompt: Before the season starts, the coach will watch each hopeful player and choose who joins the team. Nora will attend a ___. A. tournament B. tryout
application.solution: B。解析：赛季开始前通过展示能力选队员，是参加 tryout（选拔赛）。

grammar: n. 交接；（接力赛中的）递棒。可数，复数 handoffs；也可写 hand-off。
collocations: a baton handoff; a clean handoff; practice the handoff
commonMistake: handoff 是“交接”这一动作或过程；接力棒本身是 baton，二者不要混为一词。

example.english: A clean handoff helped the team keep its speed.
example.chinese: 顺畅的交接帮助队伍保持了速度。

application.prompt: The outgoing runner placed the stick directly into her teammate's hand without slowing down. Their ___ was smooth. A. handoff B. hurdle
application.solution: A。解析：跑者把棒交到队友手中的动作是 handoff（交接）。

grammar: n. 接力棒；指挥棒。可数，复数 batons；a relay baton 指接力赛中传递的短棒。
collocations: pass the baton; carry a baton; a relay baton
commonMistake: 接力赛交接的是 baton（接力棒）；handoff 指交接动作，runner 是跑者。

example.english: The runner dropped the baton near the final turn.
example.chinese: 跑者在最后一个弯道附近掉了接力棒。

application.prompt: The next runner was waiting in the exchange zone with an empty hand. The first runner passed her the ___. A. medal B. baton
application.solution: B。解析：接力跑者依次传递的短棒叫 baton（接力棒）。

grammar: n. 裁判员；法官；v. 判断、评判。过去式 judged；judgment/judgement 为名词“判断”。
collocations: a sports judge; judge a contest; judge someone by their actions
commonMistake: judge 作“判断”时不能直接接形容词作宾语；可说 judge the performance good 或 judge that it is good。

example.english: The judge gave the diver a score of nine.
example.chinese: 裁判给这名跳水运动员打了九分。

application.prompt: She watched every turn and awarded points to each skater. She was one of the ___. A. judges B. jumpers
application.solution: A。解析：负责观看动作并打分的人是 judge（裁判员）。

grammar: n. 参加赛跑的人；跑步者。由 run + -er 构成，双写 n；复数 runners。
collocations: a fast runner; a long-distance runner; a relay runner
commonMistake: run 加 -er 时双写 n：runner；run 的现在分词 running 也双写 n。

example.english: The runner crossed the finish line first.
example.chinese: 这名跑者第一个冲过终点线。

application.prompt: In the relay, each ___ ran one section of the track before passing the baton. A. run B. runner
application.solution: B。解析：句中需要表示参赛者的名词 runner；run 是动词“跑”。

grammar: phr. 领先；带头。比赛中 take the lead 指取得领先位置，过去式 took the lead。
collocations: take the lead in a race; take the lead from someone; be in the lead
commonMistake: take the lead 表示取得领先；已经领先的状态常说 be in the lead，lead 在此处是名词。

example.english: The blue team took the lead on the final lap.
example.chinese: 蓝队在最后一圈取得了领先。

application.prompt: After two runners stumbled, Mei moved ahead of everyone else. She began to ___. A. take a break B. take the lead
application.solution: B。解析：超过所有选手并跑在最前面，表示 take the lead（取得领先）。

grammar: adj. 光滑的；顺利的；平稳的。v. 使平滑；smoothly 是副词，smoothness 是名词。
collocations: a smooth surface; a smooth ride; a smooth handoff
commonMistake: smooth 作形容词修饰名词；修饰动词时要用 smoothly，如 pass the baton smoothly。

example.english: The team made a smooth change from one runner to the next.
example.chinese: 队员之间的交接很顺畅。

application.prompt: The relay runners passed the baton without dropping it or losing speed. The exchange was ___. A. smooth B. rough
application.solution: A。解析：交接没有失误也没有减速，说明 handoff 很 smooth（顺利）。

grammar: phr. 逐渐缩小与某人或某物的距离、差距。make up 后接 ground，再接 on + 对象；make 变过去式为 made。
collocations: make up ground on the leader; make up lost ground; slowly make up ground
commonMistake: make up ground on sb/sth 表示逐渐追近对方；on 后要接被追赶者，不说 make ground up on。

example.english: The cyclist made up ground on the leader during the climb.
example.chinese: 骑手在爬坡时逐渐缩小了与领骑者的距离。

application.prompt: The leader was 20 metres ahead, but Jo pedaled faster and reduced the gap. She began to ___ the leader. A. give ground to B. make up ground on
application.solution: B。解析：加速缩小与领骑者的距离，用 make up ground on（逐步追近）。

grammar: phr. 赶上；追上。catch up with 后接被追赶的人或物；catch 的过去式、过去分词是 caught。
collocations: catch up with the runner; catch up with the group; try to catch up
commonMistake: catch up with sb 表示追到对方；宾语代词放在 with 后，如 catch up with him，不说 catch him up with。

example.english: I ran faster to catch up with the group.
example.chinese: 我加快了速度，想赶上那群人。

application.prompt: The last runner increased her speed until she was beside the others. She managed to ___ them. A. catch up with B. get away from
application.solution: A。解析：跑到其他人身边、追上他们用 catch up with them。

sources.label: Cambridge Dictionary: catch up with someone

grammar: n. 花样（冰上动作）；数字；人物；v. 认为、计算。可数名词复数 figures；figure skating 指花样滑冰。
collocations: a figure on the ice; a public figure; a six-figure number
commonMistake: figure 可表示数字、人物或动作花样；figure out 表示弄明白，不能与名词 figure 的“数字”义混淆。

example.english: The skater finished her routine with a difficult figure.
example.chinese: 这名滑冰运动员以一个高难度动作结束了整套表演。

application.prompt: The skater spun, jumped, and traced a beautiful pattern on the ice. The final ___ impressed the judges. A. figure B. figurehead
application.solution: A。解析：花样滑冰中的一个特定冰上动作可称为 a figure。

grammar: n. 花样滑冰，通常不可数。figure skater 指花样滑冰运动员；比赛可说 a figure-skating competition。
collocations: compete in figure skating; figure-skating event; a figure skater
commonMistake: figure skating 是一项运动名称；skating 作此用法不加复数 -s，也不说 a figure skating。

example.english: She has trained in figure skating since she was six.
example.chinese: 她从六岁起就开始练习花样滑冰。

application.prompt: The sport combines skating with jumps, turns, and patterns on ice. She has practiced ___ for years. A. speed skating B. figure skating
application.solution: B。解析：包含跳跃、旋转和冰上图形动作的项目是 figure skating（花样滑冰）。

grammar: v. 使惊奇；使惊讶。现在分词 amazing 常修饰事物，过去分词 amazed 常描述人的感受。
collocations: amaze the audience; be amazed at; an amazing performance
commonMistake: 事物“令人惊讶”用 amazing，人的感受“感到惊讶”用 amazed；不要写成 the judges were amazing（评委很惊人）。

example.english: The young skater amazed the crowd with a perfect landing.
example.chinese: 这名年轻滑冰选手以完美落地让观众惊叹。

application.prompt: The athlete completed a triple jump without a mistake. Her performance ___ the judges. A. amazed B. tired
application.solution: A。解析：高难度动作令评委惊讶，用 amaze 的过去式 amazed，意为“使惊叹”。

grammar: adv. 真正地；诚恳地。形容词 true；true 去 e 加 -ly 构成 truly。
collocations: truly believe; truly amazing; a truly kind person
commonMistake: true 变副词时去掉 e：truly；不要按一般规则写 true-ly。

example.english: I truly believe our team can improve.
example.chinese: 我真心相信我们的队伍能够进步。

application.prompt: The coach was not just being polite; she honestly believed the young runner could win. She ___ believed in him. A. true B. truly
application.solution: B。解析：副词 truly 修饰 believed，表达“真心相信”；true 是形容词。

grammar: n. 游泳。作运动名称时通常不可数；动词 swim 的现在分词 swimming，过去式 swam，过去分词 swum。
collocations: go swimming; swimming pool; a swimming competition
commonMistake: 表示去游泳用 go swimming；swim 的现在分词双写 m：swimming，不是 swiming。

example.english: Swimming is my favorite way to exercise in summer.
example.chinese: 游泳是我夏天最喜欢的锻炼方式。

application.prompt: It is hot outside, so we plan to spend the afternoon in the pool. We are going ___. A. swimming B. running
application.solution: A。解析：在泳池里活动对应 go swimming（去游泳）。

grammar: adv. 无论如何；不管怎样；况且。常用于句首或句末，表示尽管有前述情况仍继续做某事。
collocations: try anyway; do it anyway; anyway, let's begin
commonMistake: anyway 是副词，标准写法不带 -s；表示“无论如何”不写 anyways（非正式变体）。

example.english: It started raining, but the runners finished the race anyway.
example.chinese: 虽然开始下雨了，跑者们还是完成了比赛。

application.prompt: The court was wet after the rain, but the players decided to finish the match ___. A. somewhere B. anyway
application.solution: B。解析：尽管球场湿了，选手还是决定继续比赛，用 anyway 表示“尽管如此”。

grammar: n. 典礼；仪式。可数，复数 ceremonies；形容词 ceremonial。
collocations: an opening ceremony; a medal ceremony; attend a ceremony
commonMistake: ceremony 的复数将 y 变 i 加 -es：ceremonies；不要写成 ceremonys。

example.english: The medal ceremony took place after the final race.
example.chinese: 决赛结束后举行了颁奖仪式。

application.prompt: The athletes stood on a platform while medals were presented and the anthem played. It was the award ___. A. ceremony B. audience
application.solution: A。解析：颁发奖牌、奏国歌的正式活动是 ceremony（仪式）。

grammar: det./pron. 两者都不。neither of + 复数名词作主语时，正式语法常用单数谓语；也可与 nor 构成并列结构。
collocations: neither answer; neither of them; neither one
commonMistake: neither 指两者中一个也不；说“二者都不”不再与 not 连用，以免双重否定。

example.english: Neither answer was correct, so we checked the question again.
example.chinese: 两个答案都不正确，所以我们又检查了一遍题目。

application.prompt: There were two routes to the stadium, but both were closed for repairs. ___ route was open. A. Either B. Neither
application.solution: B。解析：两个路线都关闭了，表示“两者都不开放”用 neither。

grammar: conj./adv. 也不；也没有。常与 neither 连用，也可置于否定句后构成倒装：nor + 助动词 + 主语。
collocations: neither A nor B; nor did she; nor can we
commonMistake: neither 后的并列连接词是 nor；单独放在否定句后时要倒装，如 nor did he，不说 nor he did。

example.english: He did not miss practice, nor did he arrive late.
example.chinese: 他没有缺席训练，也没有迟到。

application.prompt: The first runner did not slow down. ___ did the second. A. Nor B. So
application.solution: A。解析：前句是否定信息，补充“第二位也一样”用 nor，倒装为 nor did the second。

grammar: phr. 既不……也不……。连接两个并列成分；谓语常与靠近它的主语保持一致。
collocations: neither fast nor slow; neither A nor B; neither...nor...is/are
commonMistake: neither...nor... 本身已含否定，不能再在同一分句加 not；连接词两端的成分应保持平行。

example.english: Neither the coach nor the players were ready to leave.
example.chinese: 教练和队员们都还没有准备好离开。

application.prompt: The sports hall has no running track and no swimming pool. It has ___. A. either a track or a pool B. neither a track nor a pool
application.solution: B。解析：跑道和泳池都没有，用 neither...nor... 表示“既没有……也没有……”。

grammar: phr. 参加选拔；试用。try out for + 队伍或角色表示参加……选拔；宾语为代词时 try it out。
collocations: try out for the team; try out a new racket; try something out
commonMistake: 参加球队选拔说 try out for the team；试用物品可说 try the racket out 或 try it out，代词放中间。

example.english: Maya will try out for the volleyball team next week.
example.chinese: 玛雅下周将参加排球队选拔。

application.prompt: Leo wants a place on the school team, so he will ___ the basketball team on Tuesday. A. try out for B. look after
application.solution: A。解析：为争取进入球队而参加选拔，用 try out for the team。

grammar: adj. 独一无二的；独特的。通常不用于比较级和最高级；副词 uniquely，名词 uniqueness。
collocations: a unique style; a unique opportunity; unique to a place
commonMistake: unique 本身含“独一无二”之意，通常不用 more/most 修饰；避免写 very unique。

example.english: Each team designed a unique uniform for the event.
example.chinese: 每支队伍都为活动设计了独特的队服。

application.prompt: No other team has a uniform like ours; the pattern was designed only for us. Our uniform is ___. A. common B. unique
application.solution: B。解析：没有其他队伍拥有同样的队服，说明它是 unique（独特的）。

grammar: n. 攀岩；抱石。通常不可数，指不使用绳索、在较低岩壁或人工墙上攀爬的活动。
collocations: go bouldering; a bouldering wall; practice bouldering
commonMistake: bouldering 通常不需要绳索，常在低岩壁上进行；不要和需要绳索保护的高墙攀登混为一谈。

example.english: We tried bouldering at the indoor climbing gym.
example.chinese: 我们在室内攀岩馆尝试了抱石。

application.prompt: At the gym, Nina climbed a low wall without a rope while a padded mat covered the floor. She was doing ___. A. bouldering B. rowing
application.solution: A。解析：不系绳索、在低墙上攀爬属于 bouldering（抱石）。

grammar: v. 参加比赛；竞争。compete in + 比赛/项目；compete for + 奖项或机会；名词 competition。
collocations: compete in a race; compete for a medal; compete with others
commonMistake: 表示参加某项比赛用 compete in；争夺奖牌或名额用 compete for，介词随宾语含义变化。

example.english: Six schools will compete in the relay this year.
example.chinese: 今年将有六所学校参加接力赛。

application.prompt: The students trained for months because they wanted to take part in the city race. They will ___ in the race. A. complete B. compete
application.solution: B。解析：参加比赛并与他人争胜用 compete；complete 是“完成”。

grammar: phr. 与……竞争；和……比赛。compete against 后接对手；compete against a team。
collocations: compete against a rival; compete against other schools; compete against one another
commonMistake: against 后接竞争对手；表示参加比赛项目通常用 compete in，不要把 in 与 against 的对象互换。

example.english: Our school will compete against three strong teams.
example.chinese: 我们学校将与三支实力强劲的队伍比赛。

application.prompt: In the final, Green School will face Blue School on the court. Green School will ___ Blue School. A. compete against B. compete in
application.solution: A。解析：Blue School 是对手，因此用 compete against；compete in 后接比赛项目。

grammar: n. 吉祥物。可数，复数 mascots；常由动物或卡通形象代表队伍或活动。
collocations: a team mascot; an Olympic mascot; choose a mascot
commonMistake: mascot 是代表队伍或活动的吉祥物；它不等于 motto（口号），也不一定是真实动物。

example.english: The school mascot waved to the children before the game.
example.chinese: 比赛前，学校吉祥物向孩子们挥手。

application.prompt: A smiling tiger in a team shirt greeted fans outside the stadium. The tiger was the team's ___. A. medal B. mascot
application.solution: B。解析：代表队伍并迎接粉丝的老虎形象是 mascot（吉祥物）。

grammar: n. 口号；格言。可数，复数 mottos 或 mottoes；常表达个人或团体信念。
collocations: a school motto; live by a motto; a team motto
commonMistake: motto 是简短的信念或口号；复数可写 mottos，也可写 mottoes，不要误写成 motto's。

example.english: The team's motto is “Never give up.”
example.chinese: 这支队伍的格言是“永不放弃”。

application.prompt: The club's short guiding words are “Practice with purpose.” The club's ___ is easy to remember. A. motto B. mascot
application.solution: A。解析：用来表达团队信念的短句是 motto（格言、口号）；mascot 是吉祥物。

grammar: adj. 戏剧性的；激动人心的；巨大的。名词 drama；副词 dramatically。
collocations: a dramatic finish; a dramatic change; a dramatic performance
commonMistake: dramatic 可形容变化或结尾出乎意料、引人注目；dramatically 修饰动词，如 scores rose dramatically。

example.english: The race had a dramatic finish in the last few metres.
example.chinese: 比赛在最后几米出现了扣人心弦的结局。

application.prompt: The runner passed two rivals in the final step and won by a tiny margin. The race ended in a ___ finish. A. ordinary B. dramatic
application.solution: B。解析：最后一步反超并以微弱优势获胜，结局十分 dramatic（扣人心弦）。

grammar: n./adj. 自由式体育比赛；自由式的。游泳中 freestyle 通常指自由泳项目。
collocations: the 100-metre freestyle; a freestyle race; freestyle swimming
commonMistake: freestyle 作游泳项目名时常指自由泳；free style 分开写可表示“自由的风格”，含义不同。

example.english: He won the 100-metre freestyle at the school meet.
example.chinese: 他赢得了校运会的 100 米自由泳比赛。

application.prompt: In the pool, swimmers may choose their own stroke for this race. Ella entered the 200-metre ___. A. freestyle B. butterfly
application.solution: A。解析：允许选手自行选择泳姿的游泳项目通常称 freestyle（自由泳）。

grammar: adj. 有才能的；天才的。名词 talent；常用 be talented at/in + 名词或动名词。
collocations: a talented athlete; be talented at music; a talented young player
commonMistake: talented 是形容词，talent 是名词；说某人有才华可用 be talented at drawing 或 have a talent for drawing。

example.english: The talented runner broke the school record twice.
example.chinese: 这位有天赋的跑者两次打破了校纪录。

application.prompt: Jin learned three sports quickly and won his first race at age ten. He is a ___ young athlete. A. talent B. talented
application.solution: B。解析：名词 athlete 前要用形容词 talented（有天赋的）；talent 是名词。

grammar: phr. 惊奇地；惊叹地。常与 look、watch、stare 等动词连用，表示带着惊讶的心情。
collocations: look in wonder; watch in wonder; stare in wonder at something
commonMistake: in wonder 表示“惊奇地”这一状态；wonder 在这里是名词，不要误用形容词 wonderful。

example.english: The children watched the acrobats in wonder.
example.chinese: 孩子们惊奇地看着杂技演员。

application.prompt: The crowd watched silently as the skater jumped over a row of chairs. They watched ___. A. in wonder B. on purpose
application.solution: A。解析：观众惊叹地看着高难度跳跃，表达“惊奇地”用 in wonder。

grammar: phr. 创造纪录。set 的过去式和过去分词仍是 set；break a record 表示打破已有纪录。
collocations: set a world record; set a new record; break the record
commonMistake: set a record 表示创造纪录，动词 set 不加 -ed；打破已有纪录可说 break a record。

example.english: The swimmer set a new record in the 200-metre race.
example.chinese: 这名游泳运动员在 200 米比赛中创造了新纪录。

application.prompt: No one had ever finished the school race so quickly; the new time was the fastest on record. She managed to ___. A. make a promise B. set a record
application.solution: B。解析：创造了学校比赛最快用时，表示 set a record（创造纪录）。

grammar: n. 金；金牌；adj. 金色的、金质的。形容词 golden 常指金色的或珍贵的。
collocations: win gold; a gold medal; gold jewelry
commonMistake: win gold 表示赢得金牌，gold 在此作不可数名词；具体奖牌可说 a gold medal。

example.english: She won gold in the 400-metre race.
example.chinese: 她在 400 米比赛中获得了金牌。

application.prompt: Mina finished first in the final and stood on the top step of the podium. She won ___. A. gold B. golden
application.solution: A。解析：表示赢得金牌用 win gold；golden 是形容词，不能直接作 win 的宾语。

grammar: n. 奖章；勋章。可数，复数 medals；金牌、银牌、铜牌分别是 gold、silver、bronze medal。
collocations: win a medal; a gold medal; award someone a medal
commonMistake: medal 是可数名词，前面要有冠词或其他限定词；“赢得一枚奖牌”说 win a medal。

example.english: The runner received a medal for finishing second.
example.chinese: 这名跑者因获得第二名而拿到了一枚奖牌。

application.prompt: After placing third, Ana received a bronze ___ that hung from a ribbon around her neck. A. trophy B. medal
application.solution: B。解析：挂在颈间、颁给第三名的奖章是 medal（奖牌）；bronze medal 指铜牌。

grammar: n. 改革；变革；v. 改革、改进。可数名词复数 reforms；常用 reform a system。
collocations: education reform; reform a rule; introduce reforms
commonMistake: reform 作名词时表示改革措施，作动词时表示进行改革；不要与 perform（表演、履行）混淆。

example.english: The reform improved access to sports facilities.
example.chinese: 这项改革改善了人们使用体育设施的条件。

application.prompt: The city changed its school rules to give every child more time for sports. The new policy was an education ___. A. reform B. report
application.solution: A。解析：改变教育制度以改善学校体育条件属于 reform（改革）。

grammar: phr. 改革开放。作专名性历史表达时常指中国自 20 世纪 70 年代末开始的改革与对外开放政策。
collocations: the reform and opening-up policy; since reform and opening-up; an era of reform and opening-up
commonMistake: 固定表达中 opening-up 作名词性成分并带连字符；不要拆成 opening up 来表示“开门”。

example.english: Reform and opening-up brought major changes to the country.
example.chinese: 改革开放给国家带来了重大变化。

application.prompt: The museum display describes the policy changes that expanded economic activity and international exchange from the late 1970s. It describes ___. A. a sports meeting B. reform and opening-up
application.solution: B。解析：扩大经济活动和对外交往的历史政策通常称为 reform and opening-up（改革开放）。

grammar: adj./adv. 世界范围的；在全世界。可作定语或状语，常作定语不加连字符。
collocations: worldwide attention; a worldwide event; known worldwide
commonMistake: worldwide 作副词时前面不加介词，说 known worldwide；作形容词可说 worldwide competition。

example.english: The race attracted worldwide attention.
example.chinese: 这场比赛吸引了全世界的关注。

application.prompt: Fans in many countries watched the final online. The event became known ___. A. worldwide B. nearby
application.solution: A。解析：许多国家的观众都观看比赛，说明赛事 worldwide（在全世界范围内）受到关注。

grammar: n. 市民；公民。可数，复数 citizens；citizenship 指公民身份。
collocations: a citizen of a country; local citizens; a good citizen
commonMistake: citizen 指拥有某国公民身份的人或城市居民；city 是城市本身，二者词形相似但词性和含义不同。

example.english: Every citizen can help keep the city clean.
example.chinese: 每位市民都可以帮助保持城市整洁。

application.prompt: A person who legally belongs to a country and has its rights is a ___. A. visitor B. citizen
application.solution: B。解析：拥有一国法律身份和相应权利的人是 citizen（公民）。

grammar: n. 自豪（感）；骄傲。形容词 proud；常用 take pride in 或 be proud of。
collocations: take pride in; be proud of; a source of pride
commonMistake: pride 是名词，proud 是形容词；“为……感到自豪”可说 take pride in sth 或 be proud of sth。

example.english: The whole town felt pride in its young athletes.
example.chinese: 全镇都为年轻运动员感到自豪。

application.prompt: The volunteers cared deeply about their town's success. They took great ___ in the team's victory. A. pride B. proud
application.solution: A。解析：take great pride in 是固定搭配，表示“为……感到自豪”；pride 是名词。

grammar: n. 和谐；和睦；（音乐）和声。形容词 harmonious；通常不可数，表示一段和声时可数。
collocations: live in harmony; social harmony; sing in harmony
commonMistake: harmony 可指人际和睦，也可指音乐和声；形容词“和谐的”用 harmonious，不用 harmony。

example.english: The choir sang in harmony at the ceremony.
example.chinese: 合唱团在典礼上和谐地演唱。

application.prompt: The singers listened to one another and blended their notes beautifully. They sang in ___. A. silence B. harmony
application.solution: B。解析：歌手的音符融合得很协调，表示他们 in harmony（和谐地）演唱。

grammar: adv. 深深地；非常。形容词 deep；deeply 常修饰 feel、move、care、regret 等动词。
collocations: deeply moved; care deeply about; deeply sorry
commonMistake: deeply 常修饰抽象感受或程度；表示实际深度时也可用 deep，如 dive deep。

example.english: The story deeply moved the audience.
example.chinese: 这个故事深深打动了观众。

application.prompt: The athlete was so touched by the crowd's support that she felt it strongly. She was ___ moved. A. deeply B. deep
application.solution: A。解析：副词 deeply 修饰 moved，说明运动员“深受感动”；deep 是形容词或表示实际深度的副词。

grammar: n. 能手；主人；硕士；v. 掌握、精通。过去式 mastered；mastery 是名词“精通”。
collocations: master a skill; a master of chess; master the basics
commonMistake: master 作动词可直接接技能或知识，不需介词：master a skill；不要说 master of a skill（除非作名词）。

example.english: It took Ava years to master the violin.
example.chinese: 艾娃花了数年时间才熟练掌握小提琴演奏。

application.prompt: After daily practice, Ava could play every difficult passage with confidence. She had managed to ___ the violin. A. write B. master
application.solution: B。解析：熟练掌握乐器演奏技能用 master（精通、掌握）。

grammar: v. 使满意；满足。形容词 satisfied（感到满意的）、satisfying（令人满意的）；名词 satisfaction。
collocations: satisfy a need; satisfy the judges; be satisfied with
commonMistake: 人感到满意用 satisfied，事物令人满意用 satisfying；be satisfied 后常接 with。

example.english: The final score satisfied both teams.
example.chinese: 最终比分让两支队伍都满意。

application.prompt: The meal was exactly what the hungry runners wanted. It ___ their need for a warm dinner. A. satisfying B. satisfied
application.solution: B。解析：句子谓语需要动词过去式 satisfied，表示晚餐“满足了”跑者的需要；satisfying 是形容词。

grammar: adj. 希腊的；n. 希腊人、希腊语。首字母大写；Greece 是国家名，复数 Greeks 指希腊人。
collocations: Greek history; a Greek citizen; speak Greek
commonMistake: Greek 表示希腊的、希腊人或希腊语时首字母大写；greek 小写不能表示国籍或语言。

example.english: The athlete learned a few words of Greek before the trip.
example.chinese: 出行前，这名运动员学了几句希腊语。

application.prompt: The museum guide was born in Athens and spoke the language of Greece. She spoke ___. A. greek B. Greek
application.solution: B。解析：语言名称 Greek 必须大写首字母；greek 的小写形式不符合此处拼写规则。

grammar: adj. 古罗马的；罗马的；n. 古罗马人、罗马人；也可指罗马字体。首字母大写。
collocations: Roman history; the Roman Empire; Roman citizens
commonMistake: 表示古罗马文明或罗马人的 Roman 首字母大写；roman 小写通常指普通字体，不表示国籍。

example.english: The athletes ran past the remains of a Roman stadium.
example.chinese: 运动员们跑过一座古罗马体育场的遗址。

application.prompt: The history book describes roads built in the ancient empire centered in Rome. It describes ___ roads. A. Roman B. roman
application.solution: A。解析：形容古罗马帝国的道路，Roman 作为专名派生形容词要大写。

grammar: v.（使）淹死；溺水。过去式和过去分词 drowned；可不及物表示溺水，也可及物表示使某人溺水。
collocations: drown in a river; nearly drown; drown someone out
commonMistake: drown in water 表示溺水；drown out 表示声音盖过另一种声音，不能和“溺水”义混淆。

example.english: The lifeguard pulled the swimmer from the deep water before he could drown.
example.chinese: 救生员在游泳者可能溺水前把他从深水中拉了出来。

application.prompt: The child fell into the lake but was rescued before he lost his life underwater. He nearly ___. A. drowned B. dived
application.solution: A。解析：差点在水中丧命是 nearly drowned（差点溺水身亡）。

grammar: n. 欢呼声；v. 欢呼、喝彩；使高兴。过去式 cheered；cheerful 是形容词“高兴的”。
collocations: cheer for a team; cheer loudly; a loud cheer
commonMistake: cheer for sb 表示为某人或队伍喝彩；cheer up 表示使振作或振作起来，介词短语含义不同。

example.english: The crowd cheered for the runners as they entered the stadium.
example.chinese: 跑者进入体育场时，人群为他们欢呼。

application.prompt: The fans shouted happily when their team scored. They began to ___ for the players. A. cheer B. judge
application.solution: A。解析：球迷因队伍得分而欢呼，用 cheer for the players（为球员喝彩）。

grammar: n. 人群；观众；v. 挤满；聚集。a crowd of + 复数名词；作主语时谓语常用单数。
collocations: a large crowd; a crowd of fans; crowd around someone
commonMistake: a crowd of fans 的中心词是 crowd，作主语通常用单数谓语；crowd around 表示围聚在周围。

example.english: A large crowd gathered outside the sports hall.
example.chinese: 一大群人聚集在体育馆外。

application.prompt: Hundreds of spectators filled the square to watch the parade. A huge ___ had gathered there. A. queue B. crowd
application.solution: B。解析：聚集观看游行的许多观众构成一群人，即 a crowd。
